Commentary.Commentary: We are set to resume! The West Indies fielders have taken the field. So have Aiden Markram and Dean Elgar. Kemar Roach to start with the ball.
.. Innings 2 ...

South African bowlers started really well with Kagiso Rabada and Lungi Ngidi beating the outside edge with the new ball on several occasions. Then came on the hero of the first session, Anrich Nortje, he picked up 3 wickets in the first session to rock the Windies' top order. Kagiso Rabada also took a wicket in that session. Post Lunch though, it was all about Lungi Ngidi. The right-arm pacer bowled consistently in the corridor outside off and induced the outside edge to get his wickets. He ended with a 5-wicket haul and will be delighted with the way the series has started for him. Now, it is up to the South African batters to score a big score.

None of the Windies batters crossed the 20- run mark and that should tell you the story. Shai Hope and Kraigg Brathwaite had a good start as they survived the new ball for a while but once they fell, West Indies were in all sorts of trouble, none of their batters barring Roston Chase showed any intent to hang in there. There were a lot of poor shots and the wickets of Kyle Mayers and Rahkeem Cornwall were a result of such poor shots. The lack of foot movement also cost them as they edged a lot of balls to the slip cordon. In the end, they managed only 97. Now, it will be up to their bowlers to put on some fight.

Well, well the day so far has been all about the South African bowlers. They have dismissed the hosts for under 100 and now their batters will look to pile a lead. For West Indies, the decision to bat after winning the toss will come under scanner as they haven't even managed to score 100 runs.

OUT! TAKEN! Lungi Ngidi has taken 5 wickets in the innings! Jason Holder gets the outside edge as he looks to defend it. The ball goes to the second slip where Aiden Markram dives to his left to take the catch. West Indies end at 97 for 10!
Commentary.Howout: c Aiden Markram b Lungi Ngidi

Drinks break! South African bowlers have done well to exploit the conditions. They have managed to keep the Windies batters on the backfoot. Nortje claimed his fourth removing Blackwood soon after lunch. Ngidi entered into the wickets column by removing Raston Chase and Joshua Da Silva in quick succession. He bagged another two in the likes of Cornwall and Roach. South Africa just need a single wicket before they come to bat on.

OUT! CAUGHT! Lungi Ngidi bags his third. Pitches it a bit short, outside off. Cornwall went for the punch over point. He did not time his shot well and the ball went up in the air towards the third man region. Aiden Markram, who is standing the slip cordon, calls for it and takes an excellent catch. It is always difficult to run backward and to take a catch. Markram made it look like a piece of cake. Rahkeem Cornwall departs after an entertaining knock, he was looking really good in his short stay but he decided to hit this one out of the park. South Africa ruling over West Indies.

We are back for the post Lunch session. The South African fielders take their positions in the field. Out come Roston Chase and Jermaine Blackwood. Anrich Nortje to resume with the ball.
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

Right then! We are done with the first session on Day 1 and it has belonged to South Africa. Now, West Indies will look to build a partnership after Lunch, but will they be able to do so? Or will South Africa run through the West Indies middle order? We will find out. Do join us in a while for the post Lunch session.

The West Indies had a morning to forget. Kraigg Brathwaite and Shai Hope did the hard work of seeing off Kagiso Rabada and Lungi Ngidi in the first spell. They got lucky on a few occasions but still survived. But they were both castled by Anrich Nortje, Hope got a peach of a delivery by Nortje while Brathwaite misjudged an inswinger to lose his wickets. Nkrumah Bonner and Roston Chase hung in there with Chase showing great patience as he took 25 balls to get off the mark. But the class of Rabada was too good for Bonner as he edged one behind to the keeper. Right before Lunch, Kyle Mayers played a nothing shot to lose his wicket to Nortje. Now, it is up to Roston Chase and Jermaine Blackwood to put on a fight post Lunch.

The first session belonged to the South Africans. Rabada and Ngidi started really well with the ball and beat the openers on a number of occasions but couldn't induce the edge. That changed when Nortje came in the attack, the tall right-arm pacer removed the Windies openers in quick succession and put his team on top. Kagiso Rabada finally found the outside edge as he dismissed Nkrumah Bonner and Anrich Nortje removed Kyle Mayers just before Lunch. They will look to pick the remaining West Indies wickets as soon as possible.

A session that thoroughly belonged to South Africa. They have taken 4 wickets and are right on top of the game. For West Indies, the next session will be all about trying to get some partnerships to put on a good score.

The ball finds the outside edge this time and carries through to Quinton de Kock. He makes no mistake holding on to that one. Kagiso Rabada strikes. Nkrumah Bonner will head back to the pavilion. West Indies in deep trouble now.

Drinks break! Anrich Nortje has removed both the openers and the visitors will be very delighted with that. Kagiso Rabada and Lungi Ngidi started really well with the ball and got past the outside edge on a number of occasions at the start of the game but failed to get the outside edge. But then, Anrich Nortje came on and has taken two quick wickets to put them on top. The West Indies now need a partnership and they need a big one soon. Roston Chase comes out to bat, will he be the savior?

Fuller on middle, worked towards square leg for a single.

Length delivery, outside off. Kraigg makes no attempt to play.

Who will share the new ball? Here comes Lungi Ngidi.
Good length delivery around off, Kraigg leaves it untouched. A maiden over to get underway.
On a good length, outside off. Kraigg shoulders arms to that one.
Length delivery on middle, Kraigg blocks it out.
Length delivery, coming back in on middle and leg. Kraigg defends it watchfully.
Short leg comes in straightaway. Kyle Verreynne is the fielder there.
Good length delivery, outside off. Braithwaite leaves it alone.
A short ball to start with! Bowls a back of a length delivery on middle, Braithwaite hops into the crease and blocks it out.
We are all set to begin! The South African fielders spread out in the field. Out come the Windies openers, Kraigg Brathwaite and Shai Hope. Kagiso Rabada to start with the ball.

Aiden Markram is up for a chat, says the middle wicket looks different than the nets. Adds that they good some good batting practice prior to the game. Further adds that it is quite hot and humid but they are getting used to it.

Kyle Mayers is down for a chat, says they haven't gotten enough matches to play after the series against Sri Lanka but the team has put in some good practice sessions and is raring to go. Adds that the guys are looking forward to the challenge.

PITCH REPORT - Mike Haysman is down by the pitchside, says that there is a strong breeze coming in from the North-Eastern side. Stacy-Ann King joins him, she says that the pitch will have good carry but there may not be a lot of pace on this wicket.

Dean Elgar says they don't mind bowling first and they will look to make good use of the new ball. Adds that there are a couple of debutants in their side as Kyle Verreynne and Keegan Petersen get a game.

Kraigg Brathwaite says that the wicket looks good and they want to put some runs on the board. Adds that the guys have put in some good work and are looking forward to it. Informs that Jayden Seales is going to make his Test debut.

West Indies Playing XI - Kraigg Brathwaite (C), Shai Hope, Nkrumah Bonner, Kyle Mayers, Jermaine Blackwood, Roston Chase, Joshua Da Silva (WK), Jason Holder, Rahkeem Cornwall, Kemar Roach, Jayden Seales

South Africa Playing XI - Dean Elgar (C), Aiden Markram, Keegan Petersen, Rassie van der Dussen, Kyle Verreynne, Quinton de Kock (WK), Keshav Maharaj, Wiaan Mulder, Kagiso Rabada, Lungi Ngidi, Anrich Nortje
TOSS - Both the skippers are out in the middle for the coin toss. West Indies have won the toss and they will bat first.

Hello and welcome to the first Test between West Indies and South Africa. Both the teams have somewhat new leadership. While Kraigg Brathwaite has led West Indies before, Dean Elgar will lead his side for the first time as a captain. We are likely to see plenty of new faces in this game and it will be interesting to see how they fare. Keegan Petersen is set to make his debut and there's a possibility that Kyle Verreynne could also be handed his debut cap. Who will come out on top? How will the pitch play? We will find out. Stay tuned for toss and more updates.
